title: Dynamic Message Dispatch for Plugin Architectures
business: Developers building modular iOS applications that require third-party plugin integration without recompiling the core application.
problem: Static linking prevents the core application from invoking methods on dynamically loaded modules because the compiler lacks the necessary interface definitions at build time.
solution: Objective-C utilizes a dynamic runtime that defers method binding until execution. By sending messages to objects, the runtime searches the object's class hierarchy for a matching selector, allowing the app to interact with plugins that were not present during the initial compilation.
steps: Define a common protocol that both the host application and the plugin module adopt to ensure interface consistency.
Load the external plugin bundle into the application process at runtime using NSBundle.
Instantiate the plugin class dynamically using the runtime system.
Send messages to the instantiated object using the selector defined in the protocol.
Handle potential runtime errors using NSError if the plugin fails to respond to the expected message.
outcome: The application achieves high extensibility, enabling the loading of new features as separate bundles that communicate seamlessly with the core system via dynamic message dispatch.
limitation: Dynamic dispatch introduces a slight runtime overhead compared to static function calls. Developers can check for performance bottlenecks by profiling the application in Instruments to monitor message-sending frequency in tight loops.

questions.question: In Dynamic Message Dispatch for Plugin Architectures, how does the application interact with plugins not known at compile time?
options: By using the dynamic runtime to defer method binding until execution.
By recompiling the core application every time a plugin is added.
By using static linking to force interface definitions.
By converting all plugin methods into C-style primitive types.
questions.explanation: The Objective-C runtime allows for dynamic binding, which is essential for interacting with objects whose interfaces are resolved at runtime rather than compile time.
questions.evidence: Objective-C utilizes a dynamic runtime that defers method binding until execution. By sending messages to objects, the runtime searches the object's class hierarchy for a matching selector, allowing the app to interact with plugins that were not present during the initial compilation.

questions.question: In Dynamic Message Dispatch for Plugin Architectures, what is a primary trade-off of using dynamic dispatch?
options: It prevents the use of protocols for interface definition.
It requires manual memory management for all objects.
It introduces a slight runtime overhead compared to static calls.
It forces all errors to be handled via exceptions.
questions.explanation: Dynamic dispatch provides flexibility but incurs a performance cost because the runtime must perform a lookup for each message sent.
questions.evidence: Dynamic dispatch introduces a slight runtime overhead compared to static function calls.
